children: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) on Wednesday launched the TCS Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab, a lights-out factory at its Sahyadri Park campus in Pune.

A lights-out factory is a manufacturing unit where autonomous systems can run production with minimal human intervention. The Pune lab is the first in India to have a fully robotic battery pack assembly line, TCS said.

According to the filing, the facility will focus on autonomous factory concepts, digital simulation environments, vision AI, robotics and industrial automation, as well as software-defined engineering.

"TCS' goal is to become the world's largest AI-powered technology services company, enabling customers to transform across the entire AI value chain, from infrastructure to intelligence," the company said.

Sreenivasa Chakravarti, Global Head and Vice President of Industrial Autonomy and Engineering at TCS, said, "When we think of a manufacturing facility, we picture legacy factories and heavy equipment, that run on intense manual effort. At TCS, we are reimagining those environments and building factories for the future. With our state-of-the-art TCS Industrial Autonomy & Engineering Lab - Lights-Out Factory, we are advancing TCS' vision of engineering AI-first production systems."

"We have built a facility that can help customers turn their aspiration of lights-out manufacturing into a reality. The lab provides a tangible demonstration of how the Human + AI model can help enterprises progress from digitally enabled operations to increasingly autonomous production systems," he added.
With most IT stocks trading in the red today, TCS was trading 2.40% lower at Rs 2,201.30 on the NSE at 12:03 pm on Wednesday.

title: TCS launches India’s first AI-powered ‘lights-out’ factory in Pune
